in_text_mentions: A 47-year-old Caucasian female presented with a 5-year-history bluish-grey pigmentation of the right conjunctiva, sclera, and eyelids (Figure 1). As observed from her previous annual ophthalmic examination, the intraocular pressure never exceeded 16 mmHg, and the optic nerve head appeared normal in both eyes. Gonioscopy showed wide open and medium pigmented chamber angle with all elements of angle visible. Humphrey visual fields and optical coherence tomography findings did not show glaucoma damage. Her medical history included high blood pressure.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel 2a is H&E histology from nevus of Ota article showing pigmented dendritic melanocytes in reticular dermis as captioned, matching dermal dendritic melanocytes vocabulary term. in_text_mentions: . Perifollicular hypopigmentation was seen in 6 lesions (Figure 1d). Two lesions revealed yellowish structureless areas. As for vascular structures, serpentine vessels were observed in 2 lesions. Distribution of the dermoscopic findings was homogenous in all the lesions. Reticular pigmentation pattern was not detected in any case. Histopathologically, all of the lesions showed pigmented dendritic melanocytes and melanophages dissecting bundles of dermal collagen in reticular dermis (Figure 2a, 2b). The clinical, dermoscopic and histologic features of the patients are summarized in the Table 1.

plate_findings.evidence: darker iris in the right eye compared to the blue iris of the left eye (heterochromia iridis)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Slit-lamp photo of right eye in article titled Unilateral open-angle glaucoma associated with ipsilateral nevus of ota. Caption states folding/mammillations and darker iris/heterochromia; in-text attributes both Fig 2a and 2b to right eye darker iris and mammillations. B: Second slit-lamp view of same right eye attributed in-text to darker iris/heterochromia and mammillations in nevus of Ota case. Shows hyperpigmented iris.
panels.attribution_text: Magarasevic and Abazi. Unilateral open-angle glaucoma associated with the ipsilateral nevus of ota.. Case reports in ophthalmological medicine 2013. doi:10.1155/2013/924937. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Slit-lamp photographs show folding on the iris, more prominent in the pupil area in the right eye (mammillations) (a). The darker iris in the right eye compared to the blue iris of the left eye (b) (heterochromia iridis).
in_text_mentions: the left eye. In comparison to blue iris in the left eye, the right eye showed darker iris (heterochromia iridis) and numerous tiny pigmented nodules and folding on the iris (mammillations) (Figures 2(a) and 2(b)). Gonioscopy showed wide open and much pigmented chamber angle in the right eye than five years ago (Figure 3). In the left eye, chamber angle was wide open and not pigmented (Figure 4). In the right eye, the intense pigmentation on the external wall of the angle prevented the observation of other structures. Dilated fundus ophthalmoscopy demonstrated asymmetric “darker” pigmentation

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). B: Panel B is clinical photo showing mottled bluish-black macular pigmentation of left ala and malar region, specific captioned manifestation of nevus of Ota. panels.attribution_text: Seemongal-Dass et al. A Case of Nevus of Ota in Trinidad and Tobago.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.78311. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.

in_text_mentions: On cutaneous examination, there were multiple mottled bluish-black macular pigmented regions involving the left malar region, left upper eyelid, left ala of the nose, and the inferonasal sclera of the left eye (Figure 1). There were no pigmentary changes on other parts of the body, including nails, mucous membranes, or axillary regions.

in_text_mentions: opsy, which revealed dendritic and fusiform melanocytes in the papillary dermis, diffusely infiltrating the collagen interstitium. Additionally, melanophages extending into the reticular dermis were observed, confirming the bilateral presentation of Ota nevus based on the pathological report (Figure 2). Unfortunately, our public dermatology center does not have access to a Q-switched laser. We recommended that the patient seek treatment at a facility equipped with this technology. However, the patient was lost to follow-up, and we were unable to ascertain the outcome of her treatment decision.

plate_findings.evidence: Gray-blue macules on the left face (caption)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Left profile clinical photograph of a young woman showing gray-blue macules on the left face consistent with nevus of Ota. Caption confirms gray-blue macules and sagged subcutaneous thickening on the left face. B: Frontal clinical photograph showing gray-blue macules on the left periorbital and cheek regions consistent with nevus of Ota. Caption confirms gray-blue macules and sagged subcutaneous thickening on the left face. C: Right oblique profile clinical photograph showing gray-blue discoloration on the face. Caption groups panels A-C together as showing gray-blue macules and sagged subcutaneous thickening on the left face consistent with nevus of Ota.
panels.attribution_text: Zhong et al. Diffuse neurofibroma within nevus of Ota on the left face. JAAD case reports 2024. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.

in_text_mentions: macules on the left periorbital, temporal, jugal, and pre- and retroauricular regions, with sagged, soft, subcutaneous thickening without a clear boundary, where the skin could be pulled up manually (Fig 1, A-C). No café-au-lait macules, freckles, masses, or developmental abnormalities were observed in other parts of the body. Routine laboratory tests and a cranial computed tomography scan showed normal results.
